ACTION MINUTES
  CITY OF ALHAMBRA PLANNING COMMISSION

  Special Meeting
  May 18, 2020

A.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER:  6:30 pm in the Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

B.  ROLL CALL:
  Present:  Chan, E. Garcia, Sanchez, D. Garcia, Gardea, Messina, Sahu, Tang, Yee,
  Dunkel-Soto

  Absent:  None

  Staff Present: Vanessa Reynoso, Deputy Director, Paul Lam, Principal Planner, Scott
  Quyle, Associate Planner, Greg Murphy, Deputy City Attorney

C.  ELECTION OF OFFICERS
  • Commissioner D. Garcia nominated President Sanchez for President
  of the Planning Commission, Seconded by Commissioner Sahu.
  • The nomination carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 7-2-1
  Ayes:  Chan, D. Garcia, Gardea, Messina, Sahu, Yee,
  Dunkel-Soto
  Noes:  E. Garcia, Tang
  Abstain:  Sanchez
  Absent:  None

  •  Commissioner Tang nominated Commissioner Sahu for Vice
  President of the Planning Commission, Seconded by Commissioner
  Gardea.
  •  The nomination failed by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 4-6
  Ayes:  E. Garcia, Gardea, Sahu, Tang
  Noes:  Chan, D. Garcia, Messina, Yee, Dunkel-Soto, Sanchez
  Abstain:  None
  Absent:  None

  •  Commissioner Tang nominated Commissioner E. Garcia for Vice
  President of the Planning Commission, Seconded by Commissioner
  Sahu.
  •  The nomination carried by the following roll call vote:

  1
  5/18/2020
   Roll Call Vote: 7-2-1
  Ayes:  Chan, D. Garcia, Gardea, Sahu, Tang, Yee, Sanchez
  Noes:  Messina, Dunkel-Soto
  Abstain:  E. Garcia
  Absent:  None

  •  By majority of consent of the Planning Commission, Director of
  Community Development Marc Castagnola was nominated for
  Planning Commission Secretary.
  •  The nomination carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 9-1
  Ayes:  Chan, D. Garcia, E. Garcia, Gardea, Messina, Sahu,
  Yee, Dunkel-Soto, Sanchez
  Noes:  Tang
  Abstain:  None
  Absent:  None

D.  CONSENT AGENDA:

  ITEM 1:  MINUTES OF APRIL 29, 2019
  Recommended Action: Approve as submitted.

  ITEM 2:  MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 18, 2020
  Recommended Action: Approve as submitted.

  ITEM 3:  EXTENSION FOR CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CU-18-17,
  RESIDENTIAL PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT RP-18-18,
  COMMERCIAL PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT CP-18-17
  • Address: 123 South Chapel Avenue
  • Request: This is a request for a one-year time extension for the
  previously approved Conditional Use Permit CU-18-17, Residential
  Planned Development Permit RP-18-18, and Commercial Planned
  Development Permit CP-18-17 to develop a 37-unit mixed-use
  condominium complex on an approximate land area of 37,265 square
  feet located in the CBD (Central Business District) zone.
  • Recommended Action: Approve as submitted.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve Consent Calendar Items 1, 2, 3
  •  Moved by Commissioner Sahu, Seconded by Commissioner Yee
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 9-0-1
  2
  5/18/2020
   Ayes:  Chan, Dunkel-Soto, D. Garcia, Gardea, Messina,
  Sahu, Tang, Yee, E. Garcia, Sanchez
  Noes:  None
  Abstain:  Gardea
  Absent:  None

  •  For additional information regarding the discussion, the audio
  recording of the discussion is available here:
  https://drive.google.com/file/d/111WHwEpGL6rC1ybkV3e6D1lqnr
  BAjeDj/view).

E.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  ITEM 4:  INDUSTRIAL PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT IP-19-01 AND
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CU-19-01
  • Address: 501 South Marengo Avenue
  • Request: This is an application for an Industrial Planned
  Development Permit (IP-19-1) and Conditional Use Permit (CU-19-
  1) to develop an approximate 53,700 square foot warehouse and
  office facility for Southern California Edison Alhambra Yard. A new
  entrance will be constructed along South Raymond Avenue and new
  parking spaces to accommodate the new warehouse and office
  facility. The project is located on a site of approximately 30.7 acres
  within the Industrial Planned Development zone. A Mitigated
  Negative Declaration (MND) has been prepared for the project.
  • Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution 20-17 approving the
  Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program and Mitigated
  Negative Declaration, Industrial Planned Development Permit IP-19-
  1 and Conditional Use Permit CU-19-1 subject to the Conditions of
  Approval.
  • Associate Planner Scott Quyle provided staff presentation.
  • Commissioner Comments: Commissioners had concerns regarding
  the placement of trees on the property, the landscape along Mission
  Road, the landscape island around the proposed building, and the lack
  of a condition of approval for the installation of a new city sidewalk
  along the South Raymond Avenue as there is no sidewalk there
  currently. Victoria Loufek, applicant, responded to the Commission’s
  questions and concerns.
  • Public Comments: There were none.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to continue Industrial Planned Development Permit IP-19-01
  and Conditional Use Permit CU-19-01 to June 15, 2020.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Sahu, Seconded by Commissioner Tang.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:
  3
  5/18/2020
   Roll Call Vote: 10-0
  Ayes:  Chan, Dunkel-Soto, D. Garcia, Gardea, Messina,
  Sahu, Tang, Yee, E. Garcia, Sanchez
  Noes:  None
  Abstain:  None
  Absent:  None

  •  For additional information regarding the discussion, the audio
  recording of the discussion is available here:
  https://drive.google.com/file/d/111WHwEpGL6rC1ybkV3e6D1lqnr
  BAjeDj/view).

ITEM 5:  ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT ZTA-20-3
  • Address: All residential zoned properties
  • Request: This is an Amendment to Title 23 (Zoning) of the
  Alhambra Municipal Code to allow Accessory Dwelling Units
  (“ADUs”) and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (“JADUs”) in all
  residential zones subject to proposed standards.
  • Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution 20-14 recommending
  approval of Zone Text Amendment ZTA-20-3 to the City Council.
  • Principal Planner Paul Lam provided staff presentation.
  • Commissioner Comments: Commissioners clarified with Staff the
  requirements of the proposed ordinance. Commissioner Gardea
  cautioned that certain setback requirements may not be consistent
  with State ADU laws and suggested consultation with the State on
  that matter.
  • Public Comments: There were none.

MOTION:
  •  Moved to recommend approval of Zone Text Amendment ZTA-20-3
  to the City Council.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Sahu, Seconded by President Sanchez
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 10-0
  Ayes:  Chan, Dunkel-Soto, D. Garcia, Gardea, Messina,
  Sahu, Tang, Yee, E. Garcia, Sanchez
  Noes:  None
  Abstain:  None
  Absent:  None

  •  For additional information regarding the discussion, the audio
  recording of the discussion is available here:
  https://drive.google.com/file/d/111WHwEpGL6rC1ybkV3e6D1lqnr
  BAjeDj/view).
  4
  5/18/2020
   ITEM 6:  ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS
  • Request: The Deputy Director of Community Development will be
  providing an update regarding the status of Accessory Dwelling Units
  throughout the City.
  • Recommended Action: Planning Commission receive and file this
  informational report.
  • Deputy Director Vanessa Reynoso provided an update regarding the
  status of Accessory Dwelling Units throughout the City.
  • Commissioner Comments:
  Commissioner Sahu questioned in the Covid-19 Stay-At-Home
  orders affected ADU applications. Principal Planner Paul Lam stated
  that the number of applications and interest in developing ADUs has
  not been impacted.
  Commissioner Tang pointed out two errors in the ADU report.
  Commissioner Dunkel-Soto informed the Commission and Staff
  that ADUs will count towards affordable housing units required under
  the Regional Housing Needs Assessment.
  • Public Comments: There were none.

  •  For additional information regarding the discussion, the audio
  recording of the discussion is available here:
  https://drive.google.com/file/d/111WHwEpGL6rC1ybkV3e6D1lqnr
  BAjeDj/view).

F.  DIRECTOR’S REPORT:

  •  There was none.

G.  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

  •  There were none.

H.  COMMISSION ORALS:

  •  Commissioner Tang inquired if any Commissioners were accrued charges on their
  phone bills for calling into any City meetings as he did while calling into a City Council
  meeting. He was of the opinion that such costs could be a hinderance to the public
  process. He also asked when the Planning Commission will return to meeting publicly.
  Deputy Director Reynoso stated that was to be determined.
  •  Commissioner D. Garcia commented that the telephonic format was problematic and
  if there was any consideration for video conferencing.

  5
  5/18/2020
 I.  ADJOURNMENT:

  •  There being no other business, the meeting was adjourned at 9:30 PM.

  _______________________________
  Allen Sanchez
  President
